6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (Vidyut Artefact):
Vidyut erroneously stamps this rule at step 13 after the string is already rAmAn. This is fundamentally incorrect, as 6.1.102 (apavāda) wholly supersedes 6.1.101 (utsarga) in this specific morphological context. Our engine correctly omits it.
Where Our Engine is Right
Our engine correctly avoids Vidyut's redundant duplicate call to 1.1.73 and its erroneous, post-facto invocation of 6.1.101. The state-machine execution of the Tripādī prohibition (8.4.37) in Our Engine is structurally superior to Vidyut's late application.
notes.author: me
notes.verdict: Claude 2026-11-16 — Checked against the Vidyut trace of rāma + śas: Vidyut runs 6.1.102 (step 11), 6.1.103 (12), THEN 6.1.101 on rAmA|n (13) — the form does not change, so it is a no-op stamp (T10:no-op, R-015). Our engine rightly omits it. The duplicate 1.1.73 (Vidyut steps 6 and 7) is also real. No change.

Internal String Allocation of Ekādeśa (Minor Structural Artefact)
Step: #190
Sūtra involved: 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः.
Issue: The internal parts array [["rAmA", "prakriti", "rAma"], ["t", "sup", "At"]] reveals that instead of treating the ekādeśa as a dual-replacement spanning both boundaries (6.1.84), the engine chopped the 'ā' off the suffix At and appended it to the stem.

Classification: Display/Engine structural artefact.
notes.verdict: Claude 2026-11-16 — Repeat of a stamped note; resolved, see S184 (ekādeśa as one shared token over both sides; the parts array is a display of the split) and the 6.1.102 / 6.1.84 judgement. No new work.
